newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Asia-Pacific natural gas demand to grow at 16 pct.
newsitem.headline: Asia-Pacific natural gas demand to grow at 16 pct.

text.p: Demand for natural gas in the Asia-Pacific region is expected to grow by 16 percent between now and the year 2000, Malaysia's Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Monday.

"We... expect that demand for natural gas will expand by 16 percent between now and the year 2000, compared to four percent for oil in the same period," Anwar told the Gas Information Exchange in the Western Pacific Area (Gasex '96) conference.
The increasing use of natural gas was linked to the rapid economic growth of the region as a whole, he said.
"It is significant that the strongest growth of utilisation of gas is in the Asia-Pacific region, viewed by many as home of the world's fastest-growing economies," said Anwar.
He said there was a shift to natural gas as the preferred fuel in the region.
"Countries which previously ignored their natural gas resources are now in the process of developing the industry with an eye towards the export market."
Anwar said natural gas accounted for 22 percent of the region's energy demand, which compared with 42 percent for oil and 26 percent for coal.
